title: Kitchen sink call: John Smith
script: Happy Pipes Home Visit Field Scripts v2 (Jake, 2026-10-28), Comms base44/shared/coreScriptV2.ts; copy as read on 2026-10-28 in sim/coreScriptV2_snapshot.ts
rule: T lines are the script's words with only the [BRACKETS] filled. H lines are the script's likely replies; where the script leaves the reply open ([Tells the story], [X] years) it is filled for this call. 'adapted' marks a line changed beyond its brackets, with why. 'say' is what the voice reads when it differs from the words on screen (numbers spelled out for the phone aligner). src = step:index into that step's lines in SCRIPT_V2.

fills.WHAT THEIR ANSWER POINTS TO: water filtration and your water heater
a partly clogged drain line and a cracked trap
fills.ONE OR TWO SAFETY CONCERNS FROM THE CHEC: the seized shutoff valves under the sink
fills.FINDING x3: the seized shutoff valves, the hard water buildup, the missing drain pan under the water heater

lines.text: Hey there, you must be John?
That's me.
I'm Mike with Happy Pipes. Here's my card. We visited on the phone a little bit ago. It's good to meet you in person.
Nice to meet you too. Come on in.
I'm gonna slip these shoe covers on real quick.
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-30: the shoe covers go on the moment John asks him in, standing right there, and this is said as he starts; his thanks (S3_01) follows straight on while he puts them on. The script has the covers after the reviews (S3:4).

lines.text: I appreciate you having us out, John. I know you've got plenty of companies you could've called, so thank you for trusting us with your home.
You guys have great reviews.
Thank you. We've got a good team. Everybody here wants to serve our customers at the highest level.
I see you got to visit with Sarah when you called in. She takes good care of our customers. We're lucky to have her.
She was very friendly.
It sounds like your sink has been acting up. I've got her notes right here. So nothing gets lost between her notes and me, tell me what's been going on.
Well, it all started about two weeks ago. The kitchen sink got slow, and now every time the dishwasher runs, there's water under the cabinet.
lines.adapted: the script's reply is open ('Well, it all started when...'); filled with this call's story

lines.text: Oh no, I hate that for you.
lines.adapted: one of the script's own examples in the direction to acknowledge the emotion

lines.text: Yeah, it's been pretty frustrating.
And how long have you been in the home?
About 12 years now.
Got it. Then you know more about this home than I could ever discover in the next 30 minutes. Mind if I ask you a few more questions?
lines.say: Got it. Then you know more about this home than I could ever discover in the next thirty minutes. Mind if I ask you a few more questions?

lines.text: Sure, go ahead.
John, since you chose Happy Pipes, I'm going to get you a Guaranteed Proposal and do my best to get this taken care of today.
Anything else you can think of? Anything I should've asked and didn't?
No, I think that's everything.
I appreciate you sharing all that.

I follow an EPA checklist. While I'm working, if I spot anything that could make your home more comfortable, save you money, or cause damage or be a safety concern, would you like me to share it with you?
Sure.
Do you mind showing me to the sink? We'll get started.
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-30: "The transition is we got to get to the repair ... you mind showing me to the sink? We'll get started." The script's S5 starts as they walk to the spot, with no line for asking to be shown.

lines.text: Here it is.

Before I get started, I want to leave this with you. It's yours to keep. A lot of our customers are surprised how much more we handle than plumbing. Things that make a home more comfortable to live in.
Does anything in that guide catch your eye?
Maybe so.
No rush. Look through it while I work. If something stands out, let me know and I'll share more about it.
You're welcome to come along while I diagnose it. In fact, I'd enjoy the company. I'll walk you through everything step by step.

Here's my plan: I'll start at the kitchen sink you called about. Once I know what's going on, I'll come find you and show you what I found. Then I'll check your water heater, and I'll tag your emergency shutoffs, so in an emergency you know exactly where to shut things off. Where will you be so I can come find you?
I'll be in the living room. Come grab me.
lines.adapted: the script's reply says the kitchen; in this house the technician works at the kitchen sink and John waits on the living room sofa

lines.text: Sounds good. And where's your water heater?
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-31: he goes to the water heater after S9, so he asks where it is before then ("do you know where the water heater is, even before this occurs"). The script has no line for it; said after John says where he will be.

lines.text: It's in the coat closet, right by the front door.
lines.adapted: the reply to S6_05; in this house the game puts the electric tank heater in the coat closet off the foyer (the house's closet_electric_tank layout)

lines.text: Perfect. I'll get started.
Hey, John?
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-30: "before he enters the living room, he needs to go, Hey, John, pause, and then say his line." Said again before the last check-in (S8L).

lines.text: Good news. I found the challenge with your kitchen sink.
lines.adapted: his name comes off the front: he has just called it out (S8_00, Jake 2026-10-30)

lines.text: Oh boy, what are we looking at?

I took plenty of pictures and video so you can see it for yourself. Here's what I found: your drain line is partly clogged, so when the dishwasher drains, the water backs up and leaks out of a cracked trap under the cabinet. If that keeps up, it'll rot out the floor of the cabinet.
That sounds bad.
I know it's not the news you were hoping for, but I promise we've seen worse. In situations like this, most of our customers like to see a couple of options. I'll put those together for you.
I also found that the shutoff valves under your sink are seized up, and a couple of things that could save you some money.
Before I get started on all that, I wanted to ask you about your water.

While I was at your sink, I noticed white scale built up on the faucet and the shutoff valves. That's usually a sign of what's in the water. Are you seeing that buildup anywhere else in the home? Any odd taste or smell, anything like that?
lines.adapted: the script's direct question is about corrosion at the water heater; on this call the finding is scale at the sink. Jake 2026-10-31: having just said he saw it on the faucet he does not ask about the faucets again: "are you seeing this buildup in other places of home? Any bad water quality, any, you know, odd taste, anything like that"

lines.text: Now that you mention it, the shower heads get crusty, and the glasses come out of the dishwasher cloudy.
lines.adapted: the script leaves the reply open ([Shares what they've noticed.])

lines.text: Thank you for sharing that. Let me take a quick look at your water heater, and I'll come right back.
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-31: "He told him he was going to go to the water heater, so he needs to go to the water heater." He now walks to it (the coat closet) and back. Hard water points to the heater (scale in the tank); the water filtration (round 3j) came out of the line because in this house it is outside, by the meter at the street, and he does not go out there

lines.text: Okay, that's what I've looked at so far. I've got everything put together. Is there a place we could sit for a second?
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-31: "it's a bit off when he says this is everything I want to look at today ... He needs to actually say ... okay, that's what I've looked at so far. I've got everything put together, because the tech already has everything put together before he comes and speaks with John." He puts it together on his tablet at the water heater, before he comes back

lines.text: Sure, let's sit at the kitchen table.
lines.adapted: the script gives no reply here

lines.text: When I got here, you shared that your kitchen sink had been draining slow and leaking under the cabinet for about two weeks.
lines.adapted: Jake 2026-10-31: the script's "I wrote it down right here" is not said ("shouldn't say, I wrote it down right here at the table")

lines.text: Yes, that's right. It's been getting worse.
I was able to pin down exactly what's going on and what kind of repair it needs. Like I showed you, your drain line is partly clogged, and the trap under your sink is cracked.
This one's a significant investment. The good news is I do have the part on the truck. I am able to take care of it today. A repair like this usually takes about 60 minutes.
lines.say: This one's a significant investment. The good news is I do have the part on the truck. I am able to take care of it today. A repair like this usually takes about sixty minutes.

lines.text: Okay, that sounds great.
Together, we also found the seized shutoff valves, the hard water buildup, and the missing drain pan under your water heater.
